dct_description_sm: The OMI Cloud Pressure layer indicates the effective cloud pressure (in fact, a cloud scattering layer mean pressure), and is measured in hectopascals (hPa). The retrieved cloud cover and pressure are used to estimate, and correct for, the amount of trace gas hidden below the clouds.

The Ozone Monitoring Instrument (OMI) instrument on board the Aura satellite. The OMI Cloud Pressure layer is a science parameter of the OMI Cloud Pressure and Fraction (Raman Scattering) dataset. The sensor resolution is 25 km, imagery resolution is 2 km, and the temporal resolution is daily.

A daily visualization from NASA's Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS), available from 2005-01-01 and updated as new data arrive. Made from OMI/Aura Effective Cloud Pressure and Fraction (Raman Scattering) 1-Orbit L2 Swath 13x24 km V003 (OMCLDRR) (OMCLDRR, version 003, doi:10.5067/Aura/OMI/DATA2010).
